To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(a) metaphor chains are organized in clusters, (b) clusters are organized around the three meta-functions of language, i.e. ideation (conceptualizing reality), interperson (persuasion and manipulation), and text (text structuring), (c) clusters are organized in the order of the three meta-functions, i.e. interperson, ideation, and then text, (d) clusters are organized according to the cognitive scenarios of the target domain, i.e. marketing,

the metaphors in our corpus of marketing texts can be divided into two groups: metaphors that are used for the purpose of describing and explaining the phenomenon of marketing and metaphors that are employed to persuade the reader to buy a certain product or service.
the metaphor chains in the text are organized around a central scenario, that of a market as an organism.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the question how metaphor works in text.
the following questions: What is the role of metaphor in text?
the question of how metaphoric language is structured in texts.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
conceptual metaphor analysis is a useful and powerful tool for investigating the structure and meaning of a text.
metaphorical expressions serve different functions at different points of a text.

metaphor chains in text are not only organized according to the cognitive scenarios that are activated, but also in a way that serves the three Hallidayean metafunctions of language: interpersonal, textual and ideational.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
metaphor is a powerful and flexible tool for the construction of meaning in texts.
the metaphor chains we found in our text were multifunctional in the sense of Halliday's (1985/1994) three meta-functions: ideational, interpersonal and textual.
metaphorical expressions in texts are multifunctional, that is, that they serve more than one meta-functional purpose in a given text, and that they are organized in chains across text.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the analysis of conceptual metaphor in discourse is not a matter of identifying metaphoric expressions in isolation, but rather of analyzing the organization and multifunc- tionality of those expressions in chains.
the analysis of metaphor chains and their multifunctionality is a useful approach to the analysis of metaphor.
the multifunctionality of conceptual metaphor is best captured in the three-dimensional model of the interpersonal, the ideational and the textual metafunctions of language.
